channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Malaysia seizes $12.1M in AI chips at its main airport: falsely declared servers and a suspected smuggling syndicate
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Malaysian customs said on October 28 it had seized about 49.5 million ringgit ($12.11 million) in advanced AI chips this month, after finding 30 server units at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s free trade zone on October 15 — servers falsely declared as electronic components, in a case linked to at least five others worth more than 100 million ringgit in total.

item.title: South Korea will put 1,700 AI robots to work in the public sector — defense, firefighting and policing first
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: South Korea plans to distribute more than 1,700 AI robots across the public sector next year, starting with a two-day briefing at Seoul’s SETEC where nine government institutions will test wheeled and quadruped robots from 11 domestic makers against real field jobs in defense, firefighting and law enforcement.

item.title: Build a working multi-agent system with the OpenAI Agents SDK: tools, handoffs, guardrails, and offline tests
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The OpenAI Agents SDK turns a support desk into five primitives: agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, and sessions. This guide builds a triage system with billing, refunds, and orders specialists, wires safety checks at the boundaries where they actually run, and tests it all with no API key, verified on openai-agents 0.24.0.

item.title: Kicked out of gamedev forums for using AI, a 19-year veteran showed exactly how Claude built his farming game
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A developer with 19 years of game-making behind him says gamedev forums removed his game for its AI use — so he posted the full recipe: Claude Code writing the C#, an AI agent driving the Unity editor, and AI tools for art and models. The thread, and the game’s Steam page, show what “AI-made” actually means in practice.

item.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google’s AI chips: the ChatGPT maker moves from renting TPUs to owning them
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI plans to buy Google’s AI chips, according to a report from The Information — moving from renting Google’s TPUs to owning them, and giving the ChatGPT maker a second silicon supplier beside Nvidia.

item.title: DistillerSR launches Smart Chat: an AI chat that only answers from your own validated evidence
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DistillerSR launched Smart Chat on October 27, 2026, an AI chat interface built into its evidence platform that answers only from a customer's own DistillerSR projects — no open web, no external sources, and no separate LLM licence or setup.

item.title: Hyphenate raises $45M: self-learning finance agents that run 90% of routine work — after 86× revenue growth
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Hyphenate, the autonomous finance platform formerly known as Maximor, raised a $45 million Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners on October 27, 2026, after growing revenue 86× in a year — its agents now run 90% of routine finance work at customer companies.

item.title: Run a multi-agent trading desk on your own machine: hands-on with TradingAgents and Ollama
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: TradingAgents turns one ticker into a full research firm — analysts, bull-versus-bear debate, trader, risk team, portfolio manager — and version 0.7.1 runs it all against a local model. This guide installs it, runs NVIDIA through the whole firm on Ollama with no API keys, and shows exactly where the tiny local model can and cannot be trusted.

item.title: Cerebras brings its fast inference to Oracle Cloud: wafer-scale speed for agents, coming to OCI in 2027
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Cerebras Systems and Oracle have announced plans to bring Cerebras' fast inference service to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, giving Oracle's enterprise customers a new ultrafast option for agent workloads — with availability pencilled in for 2027, not tomorrow.

item.title: Apple opens Pages, Keynote and Numbers to outside AI agents: MCP support and OpenAI-backed assistants arrive in November
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Apple announced on October 27, 2026 that Keynote, Pages and Numbers will gain beta AI assistants built on Apple models and OpenAI, plus Model Context Protocol support letting external AI agents read, edit and automate work in the apps — a November Creator Studio update that turns Apple's office suite into an agent surface.

item.title: Call an agent like a function: a hands-on guide to Chaos Intelligence
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Chaos Intelligence (Cattmonkey/ChaosIntelligence, 202 GitHub stars in its first four days, v0.154.4) is a programming language where agents are callable values, just like functions. This guide unpacks the project ZIP, runs the bundled program, and builds three small programs — no model, no API key, no GPU — then shows where a live model call would fit, and what it costs.

item.title: Dayforce launches an agentic workforce planner: start with the work, then decide who — person or AI — does it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Dayforce announced its Strategic Workforce Planning Agent on October 27, 2026, a conversational agent that models skills, capacity and cost — including AI token costs — so leaders can decide what people, agents, or both should do, ahead of its expected availability in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: From messy PDFs to structured Markdown your retriever can cite: a hands-on guide to Docling
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Docling turns PDFs, Word files, slides and spreadsheets into structured Markdown, JSON and chunks your retriever can actually cite. This guide installs Docling 2.143.1, converts a real Word report and its PDF, inspects the tables and headings the parser recovered, tunes the pipeline, and chunks the result for RAG — every command run, every output shown.

item.title: General Compute raises $100M at an $800M valuation — for a non-Nvidia inference cloud
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: General Compute announced a $100 million Series A on October 27, 2026, co-led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures, valuing the inference-focused neocloud at $800 million post-money — up from $60 million after its May seed round — on the back of a $100 million annual-recurring-revenue customer deal.

item.title: Let an AI agent cut your video: hands-on with Concat, the free local CapCut replacement
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Concat is a free, open-source video editor that runs entirely on your own machine — and version 0.2.8 ships a built-in MCP server, so a coding agent can drive the same engine the window uses. This guide installs 0.2.8, builds a two-clip edit with a title through MCP calls, and exports a real H.264 file — every command run, every output shown.

item.title: Texas sues OpenAI over ChatGPT and minors: Paxton wants a court-approved evaluator for every new model
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman on October 23, accusing them of misleading Texans about ChatGPT's safety for children — and asking a court to bar the chatbot for minors and to vet every future model before Texans can use it.

item.title: Globant launches Glob.AI OS: an operating system for enterprise AI, routing work to 320+ models
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Globant expanded its Glob.AI platform on October 27, 2026, with Glob.AI OS, a unified governance layer that routes each task to the most cost-efficient of 320+ AI models from 25+ providers, with budgets, audit trails and human-supervised AI Pods — and charges for outcomes, not hours or seats.

item.title: Lockheed Martin Canada puts C$10M into iMAPLE, an AI that matches the right maintainer to every Hercules job
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Lockheed Martin Canada announced a C$10 million contract with Contextere on October 27, 2026, to advance iMAPLE, an AI platform for maintenance competency and workforce readiness, starting with the Royal Canadian Air Force's CC-130J Hercules fleet.

item.title: Calix releases an 8B telecom AI model on Hugging Face — its ‘Gems’ specialists arrive in 2027
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Calix released a communications language model on Hugging Face on October 27, 2026, built on an 8-billion-parameter open-weight Llama model fine-tuned for broadband networks. In 2027, specialized versions called Calix Gems will bring that expertise to the network edge, the access network, and the cloud.

item.title: Infisical raises $40M at a $600M valuation to lock down AI agents — without ever handing them the keys
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Infisical announced a $40 million Series B at a $600 million valuation on October 27, 2026, led by Elad Gil, to expand Agent Vault — a product that lets AI agents work inside enterprise systems without ever receiving the underlying passwords, API keys, or tokens.

item.title: Oracle and OpenAI bring ChatGPT and Codex into the enterprise stack
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Oracle unveiled four products with OpenAI at Oracle AI World on October 27, 2026: a ChatGPT workspace wired into its business applications, an AI-driven security testing service, a no-code app builder, and a small-business bundle with $12,000 in annual cloud credits.

item.title: Run a private, Claude-style AI coworker on your own machine: hands-on with Hob
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app that runs open-weight models entirely on your computer — no account, no subscription, and no telemetry. This guide installs Hob 0.2.1, lets it pick the model your hardware can actually run, and puts it to work on a real spreadsheet before taking it fully offline.

item.title: Liquid AI launches LFM3: six open-weight 2B-class models on one shared backbone
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Liquid AI announced LFM3 on October 27, 2026: six open-weight models in the 2B parameter range — text, vision, audio, omni, and two decision models — all branched from a single shared backbone, built to be fine-tuned on one GPU and run on phones, laptops, and edge hardware.

item.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4: a world model that talks back, with native audio and live steering
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27, 2026, its new world model for real-time interactive simulation — the first in the series to generate audio natively, so simulated worlds now sound, speak, and respond to typed steering as they unfold.

item.title: Build typed, testable AI agents with Pydantic AI: tools, structured output, and tests that run without an API key
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Pydantic AI turns an agent's output into a contract: a Pydantic model the model must satisfy, tools built from typed functions, and test models that let you prove it all without an API key. This guide builds a support-ticket triage agent and tests it three ways, all verified on Pydantic AI 2.62.0.
